query_text: Have any new literary genres emerged in this century?

action.query: 21st century emerging literary genres cli-fi litRPG new adult Twitterature

content.text:
Yes—but with a caveat: **truly “new” genres are rare**. Most 21st-century “new genres” are better understood as **new labels, market categories, or hybrids** that crystallized around new technologies, social conditions, and readerships. Still, several have clearly emerged or become recognizable this century.

### Notable 21st-century emerging genres/subgenres

| Genre / label | What it is | Why it feels new |
|---|---|---|
| **Cli-fi / climate fiction** | Fiction centered on climate change, ecological crisis, or climate-altered futures. | While environmental fiction is older, “cli-fi” became a prominent 21st-century category, especially from the 2000s–2010s onward, as climate change became a major literary subject. ([good.is](https://www.good.is/articles/climate-fiction-cli-fi-genre?utm_source=openai)) |
| **LitRPG** | Fiction that incorporates role-playing game mechanics—levels, stats, quests, inventories—into the narrative world. | It grows directly out of video-game and MMORPG culture, and the term/genre has become increasingly visible in online and audiobook publishing. ([bookbrowse.com](https://www.bookbrowse.com/blogs/editor/index.cfm/2025/1/21/LitRPG?utm_source=openai)) |
| **New Adult** | Fiction about protagonists roughly in the post–high-school to late-20s stage, often dealing with college, first jobs, sex, identity, and independence. | The label was popularized around 2009–2013 and became a publishing/marketing category, especially in romance and self-publishing communities. ([diggitmagazine.com](https://www.diggitmagazine.com/new-adult-fiction?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Twitterature / social-media literature** | Literary works shaped by platforms like Twitter/X, Instagram, blogs, or other short-form digital media. | The form depends on digital platforms, character limits, feeds, hashtags, and networked reading practices. ([philpapers.org](https://philpapers.org/rec/AGRTAN?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Instapoetry** | Short, visually simple, highly shareable poetry associated with Instagram and similar platforms. | Poetry itself is ancient, but this mode is shaped by social-media aesthetics, shareability, and direct audience engagement. Electronic-literature surveys often discuss Instapoetry and Twitterature as newer digital literary practices. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_literature?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Hopepunk** | Speculative fiction emphasizing resistance, kindness, solidarity, and hope in the face of grim systems or futures. | It emerged partly as a reaction against grimdark and dystopian storytelling; it is more a tonal/moral movement than a strict genre. |
| **Romantasy** | A hybrid of romance and fantasy where the romantic arc is as central as the fantasy plot. | Fantasy romance existed before, but “romantasy” has become a major 21st-century publishing and fan-market label. |
| **New Weird** | A revival/hybrid of weird fiction, fantasy, horror, and speculative urban strangeness, associated with writers like China Miéville and Jeff VanderMeer. | Its roots are older, but the “New Weird” label became strongly associated with early-21st-century literary speculative fiction. ([ebsco.com](https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/literature-and-writing/new-weird-literary-movement?utm_source=openai)) |

### So, have *new* genres emerged?

**Yes, especially in three ways:**

1. **Technology-created forms**  
   Social media, hypertext, fan platforms, games, and interactive media have produced or reshaped genres such as Twitterature, Instapoetry, electronic literature, LitRPG, and web-serial fiction.

2. **New social anxieties and realities**  
   Climate change helped consolidate cli-fi; economic precarity and delayed adulthood helped New Adult fiction resonate; digital alienation and platform life influence many contemporary forms.

3. **Hybridization and rebranding**  
   Many “new” genres are combinations of older ones: romantasy = romance + fantasy; hopepunk = speculative fiction + ethical optimism; New Weird = weird fiction + horror + fantasy + literary experimentation.

In short: **the 21st century has produced fewer wholly unprecedented genres than newly visible genre ecosystems**—often born from digital culture, fan communities, climate consciousness, and publishing-market labels.
